svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Create the deliberately expired leaf at the CA
Practice CA server (TLS-CA01) · RHEL 9 Bash terminal · learner@10.90.0.20
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-ca01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
bash -n ~/make-expired-fixture.sh
less ~/make-expired-fixture.sh
bash ~/make-expired-fixture.sh
openssl x509 -in ~/tls-ca/public/app-expired.crt -noout -dates -subject -issuer
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
The public fixture’s notAfter is yesterday in UTC. Its name is app.example.mil and it matches
v1.key, not v3.key.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. At the CA terminal, run bash -n first to check the script syntax, then read it with less; press q to
leave less.
2. Run the script only on your disposable practice CA. It creates separate expired-fixture database
files and signs the original v1 CSR with dates from two days ago to one day ago.
3. Enter the intermediate CA passphrase only at the prompt. No new private key is generated or copied by
this helper.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
